chunks: My father (peace be upon him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from al-Qasim ibn Yahya, from his grandfather al-Hasan ibn Rashid, from Ya'qub ibn Ja'far ibn Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Ja'fari, who said: I heard Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying:

Whoever keeps an 'Ateeq horse tied up, three sins will be erased for him every day and twenty-one good deeds will be recorded for him. And whoever keeps a 'Hajin horse tied up, two sins will be erased for him every day and seven good deeds will be recorded for him. And whoever keeps a 'Birzaun horse tied up, intending by it beauty and fulfilling needs and repelling an enemy from himself, one sin will be erased for him every day and six good deeds will be recorded for him.

key_terms.فَرَسًا عَتِیقًا: A noble or pure breed of horse

ai.seo_question: What are the daily spiritual rewards for keeping different types of horses for jihad?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-Amal* highlights the tangible spiritual benefits of maintaining horses for jihad, reflecting the practical realities of early Islamic military life where equine readiness was a communal duty. The graded rewards—ranging from erasing sins to accumulating daily good deeds—underscore the value placed on utility and readiness in Shia jurisprudence, linking physical preparation with spiritual purification.
